timezone: America/Chicago; raw samples and most actions use UTC on October 25
scope: Additional RAM stress tests for the installer integrity fix; diagnostic, not full release qualification
source_note: The full diagnostic ISO retains the published October 22 base and locked dependencies, with the integrity product changes from this PR. This follow-up changes documentation and a Rust doc comment only; it does not claim a newly built current-main ISO.

diagnostic_image.source_modifications: installer integrity checks and mandatory squashfs verification only
diagnostic_image.qualification: Diagnostic only; no release or publication approval

environment.firmware: OVMF 202608, retained variables across live and disk-only boots
environment.virtual_hardware: KVM, q35, 4 host vCPUs, virtio GPU at original 1280x800, read-only USB ISO, disposable 80 GiB NVMe raw file
environment.network: QEMU user networking; no host folders or host devices shared. Disk-only diagnostics use a loopback-only SSH forward; SSH was enabled through the normal installer GUI.
environment.live_swap: Unmodified ISO zram: approximately 1961 MiB with 2 GiB guest RAM and 3909 MiB with 4 GiB guest RAM
environment.host_load: Other workstation workloads were present; timings are diagnostic observations, not performance benchmarks
environment.synthetic_account: Disposable test account only; no personal credentials or Wi-Fi profiles. Raw input traces stay local.
environment.target_initialization: New sparse raw file, with ASCII SEKKA DISPOSABLE RAM STRESS TEST TARGET followed by newline at byte zero; all remaining bytes zero

pressure_method.allocation: 1536 separate bytearrays of 1 MiB from os.urandom; XOR one byte of every 4096-byte page every two seconds
pressure_method.service: systemd-run sekka-memory-pressure, MemoryMax=1800M, MemorySwapMax=0, existing ISO Python interpreter
pressure_method.meaning: A large incompressible resident background application. No fabricated /proc/meminfo values, Nix reports, installer settings or target-build decisions.
pressure_method.lifetime: Ready before the first GUI action; held through background verification, evaluation, confirmation, target build, bootloader and the completion screen; stopped after evidence collection.
pressure_method.sampler: Every two seconds, record /proc/meminfo, memory PSI, vmstat counters, zram stats, Nix RSS/swap and pressure cgroup bytes/events. Sampling can be delayed by extreme pressure; observed minima are sampled values.
program: # Keep 1.5 GiB of incompressible anonymous memory resident in a separate cgroup
# with MemorySwapMax=0. This models a large background application without
# changing the installer, its settings, Nix's reports, or /proc/meminfo.
print('ready: holding 1610612736 bytes of random data', flush=True)

corrupt_2g.definition: Refuse corrupted Firefox before target writes, not complete an installation
corrupt_2g.action: In the booted diagnostic ISO overlay, change Firefox application.ini version 158.0 to 158.1, preserving its size. Invoke the real packaged helper with a confirmed Aizome/Firefox installation request.
corrupt_2g.result: All 3644 paths checked; modified Firefox reported with expected/actual hashes; helper exits 1; no Prepared or Progress/formatting event; root-only integrity log retained.
corrupt_2g.target_assertion: Independently measured SHA-256 of every byte before and after; equal
corrupt_2g.caveat: The first monitoring run had a broken sampler. It was retained but excluded from RAM measurements; the corrected repeat reused that boot and may have warmed/reclaimed caches. The separate clean 2 GiB test used a fresh boot and target.

clean_2g.definition: Complete clean Aizome/Firefox installation at 2 GiB RAM
clean_2g.action: Fresh diagnostic-ISO boot and target; real packaged helper, same configuration as public control, ext4/UEFI, tuning on, target swap disabled. No pressure process or store mutation.
clean_2g.result: Live verification passed in 114.913 seconds. During subsequent Nix evaluation, zram filled, a live-store source extraction returned ENOSPC, and kernel OOM killed plasmashell. Never reached Prepared or formatting.
clean_2g.termination: After observing and preserving OOM/thrashing evidence, operator sent SIGINT to the guest evaluation process group. Final helper exit 1 includes interrupted-by-user; do not count this as automatic graceful low-memory rejection.
clean_2g.target_assertion: Entire final 80 GiB file equals the expected marked-empty target hash. There was no separate pre-run hash for this fresh file.
clean_2g.attribution: Failure occurred after the new verification stage. The unmodified public control reproduces it; this is not evidence that the integrity patch introduced the low-memory failure.

public_control_2g.definition: Complete the same clean 2 GiB installation on the unmodified public ISO
public_control_2g.action: Fresh boot of the exact public ISO with matching published SHA-256; same virtual hardware, target generator and helper request as clean_2g; no corruption or pressure service.
public_control_2g.result: Nix evaluation filled zram and failed a live-store source extraction with ENOSPC. Kernel OOM killed plasmashell and later the autostart Genkan GUI. No target formatting.
public_control_2g.termination: Operator SIGINT after the first confirmed OOM; completion was delayed during thrashing. A later SIGKILL attempt found the evaluation process group already gone. Final helper exit 1 includes interrupted-by-user.
public_control_2g.target_assertion: Entire final 80 GiB file equals expected marked-empty target hash; no independent pre-run hash.
public_control_2g.attribution: Confirms the tested public revision already fails this 2 GiB case. Current-main full-image behavior was not retested.

gui_4g_pressure.definition: Complete normal GUI installation under sustained resident pressure, exercise the real deferred route, then disk-only boot/login/Firefox
gui_4g_pressure.configuration: UEFI/NVMe/ext4, Aizome and Firefox, tuning on, default 4 GiB target swap, en_US.UTF-8, US keyboard, America/Chicago, hostname pressure-test; SSH selected through GUI
gui_4g_pressure.interaction: Actual QMP mouse/keyboard actions through welcome, disk, account, GitHub/SSH, desktop, applications, location, review/confirmation and installation. Normal greeter password entry and application-menu Firefox launch after disk-only boot.
gui_4g_pressure.deferred_proof: Review screen explicitly says build on new disk because downloads exceed available memory; saved install.json has prepared.deferred=true and cached_bytes=0; observed nix build --store local?root=<target> command.
gui_4g_pressure.disk_only_boot: Same 4096 MiB RAM; ISO and pressure service absent. Installed disk and retained firmware only, no host shares. Normal Aizome greeter/password login reached the desktop.
gui_4g_pressure.firefox_launch: Firefox opened from Toolchest > Applications > Internet > Firefox; original-resolution screenshot inspected.
gui_4g_pressure.shutdown: Normal desktop Session > Shut Down opened its confirmation dialog; its 60-second countdown shut down the VM before a later confirmation click could be sent. QEMU exited.
gui_4g_pressure.limits: Synthetic pressure installation diagnostic, not a certification of all 4 GiB computers. The artificial pressure load was not carried into the installed-system boot.

interpretation: The whole installed system need not fit into physical RAM: a measured 8.31 GiB closure installed with 4 GiB RAM while another 1.5 GiB remained resident, using the actual deferred target-build route.
The new integrity check completed under pressure and safely rejected corruption at 2 GiB. It does not solve memory requirements of Nix evaluation or space requirements of its RAM-backed live store.
Do not call 2 GiB installation reliable based on these results. Both tested images failed that case. An explicit low-memory installation strategy remains unresolved; this PR does not implement one.
Live zram was enabled as shipped. This is not a zero-swap test, a sustained hardware memory test, or proof against RAM/media faults.
No runtime changes were made after these tests. Only the inaccurate deferred-summary doc comment was corrected and this evidence was added.
fixture_notes: The first 2 GiB corruption sampler lacked PATH and repeatedly printed command-not-found errors. Stopped it, retained its 23 MB log, removed the guest log to free its RAM-backed space, added explicit PATH/set -eu, then repeated. Only the corrected sampler contributes measurements.

Fast QMP typing at 75 ms lost characters under background pressure. Cleared/refilled the account fields with 250 ms spacing and 100 ms key hold; validation succeeded. This is recorded as an automation timing correction, not attributed as a product defect.

A public-control QGA diagnostic timed out under severe pressure. A concurrent signal request encountered a stale agent reply; subsequent guest-sync resynchronization retained the replies. Retrieved the actual SIGINT status, final helper result and logs; did not infer completion from the earlier timeout.

The nested disk-boot QMP socket path exceeded AF_UNIX length despite a short symlink destination. Resolved the symlink in the host controller and retried the screenshot; guest image/settings were unchanged.

The sampler includes pressure allocation ramp-up before GUI interaction. Its whole-run minimum cgroup bytes is therefore below the final load; a separate assertion checks every sample after the first GUI action is at least 1.5 GiB.

The installed desktop shutdown dialog completed its normal countdown before the explicit confirmation click. That later QMP click failed because QEMU had already exited; it is not credited as a delivered input.
Samples are observations, not guaranteed maxima/minima. Public-control sampling slowed markedly during thrashing; kernel OOM logs independently establish failure.
